attempts.rationale: The buffer overflow occurs because `mz_zip_mem_read_func` reads beyond the allocated memory when `file_ofs + s` exceeds `pZip->m_archive_size`. Although `s` is computed as `MZ_MIN(pZip->m_archive_size - file_ofs, n)`, an integer underflow can happen if `file_ofs > pZip->m_archive_size`, causing `pZip->m_archive_size - file_ofs` to wrap around to a large value due to unsigned arithmetic. The fix adds an explicit check to ensure `file_ofs <= pZip->m_archive_size` before computing `s`, preventing the underflow and ensuring no out-of-bounds read.

attempts.rationale: The buffer overflow occurs in `mz_zip_mem_read_func` when reading beyond the allocated memory due to an integer underflow in the calculation of the remaining size. Although the code attempts to clamp the read size `s` using `(file_ofs >= pZip->m_archive_size) ? 0 : (size_t)MZ_MIN(pZip->m_archive_size - file_ofs, n)`, the subtraction `pZip->m_archive_size - file_ofs` can underflow when `file_ofs > pZip->m_archive_size` (due to unsigned integer wraparound), leading to a large value for `s` and subsequent out-of-bounds read. The fix adds an explicit check to ensure `file_ofs <= pZip->m_archive_size` before performing the subtraction, preventing the underflow. This is functionally equivalent to the original intent but avoids relying on the ternary condition alone, which may not prevent underflow in all cases due to how the condition is evaluated.
